chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
The cattle of the livestock: its owner is not liable for any compensation as long as they are left free to roam.

key_terms.يَغْرَمُ: To be liable / to pay compensation

ai.seo_question: When is an owner not liable for damages caused by their livestock?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the principle of 'gharamah' (liability for damages), exempting owners from financial compensation when livestock roam freely in common grazing lands ('mursalah'), provided no negligence is present. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling highlights the distinction between natural animal behavior in open spaces and damage caused by specific human control or confinement, serving as a foundational text for civil liability (Daman) in Islamic law. It underscores the balance between property rights and communal land use, a key consideration in classical fiqh discussions on torts.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from a man, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘The animals, cattle, its owner would not be fined for as long as they are left free to roam’.
